summary: Kootenai NF lookout: camp about 1914, platform 1921, pole tower 1924 (height disputed), L-4 tower 1949; gone by 1981; firelookout.com says the log cabin is still there.

facts.design: 40' platform between 3 trees (1921); 55' pole tower with 7x7' cab (1924); 41' treated timber L-4 tower (1949)
facts.status_note: Tower gone by 1981 per firelookout.com; the same undated page says the 1924 replacement log cabin is still there

events.note: 40' platform between three trees, with log cabin living quarters
55' pole tower with 7x7' cab and a replacement log cabin; the Inter Lake reported a 70-foot tower the same year
Tower gone by 1981; the year is the latest date given

evidence.supports: camp about 1914; 40' platform and log cabin built in 1921
evidence.quote: Established as a camp about 1914, a 40' platform between 3 trees was built in 1921 along with log cabin living quarters

evidence.supports: 55' pole tower with 7x7' cab and replacement log cabin added in 1924; log cabin still there per the page
evidence.quote: In 1924, a 55' pole tower with 7x7' cab and a replacement log cabin (still there) were added
followed by a 41' treated timber L-4 tower in 1949

evidence.supports: Kalispell Daily Inter Lake item of 1924 reports a 70-foot tower on Pinkham ridge
evidence.quote: Eureka--Forest Service builds 70-foot lookout tower on Pinkham ridge, giving excellent lookout view for fire service.

evidence.supports: item is from the Kalispell Daily Inter Lake
Montana list marks the tower gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief's 21.3 m (70 ft) matches the 1924 Inter Lake figure quoted on Forest Lookouts. firelookout.com gives 55 ft for the 1924 pole tower and 41 ft for the 1949 L-4. height_m is left out of facts; the story reports both figures and says the sources disagree.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 21.3 (70 ft) comes from the 1924 Inter Lake item, as quoted on Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com gives 55 ft for the 1924 pole tower, so the editor should decide whether to keep 21.3 after checking the newspaper itself. The firelookout.com page is undated, so its still-there cabin remark may be old. No staffing, fire or access information was found. Access is left out of facts.
